body.statement: For rational \(\mathcal O_G\) of entry height at most \(L_{\mathrm{bits}}\), use the fraction-free immutable-row handle to determine whether exact-once enumeration admits total bit complexity polynomial in \(p,m,L_{\mathrm{bits}},2^p,N_{\mathrm{out}}\) and the emitted encoding length, including canonical equality certificates for interned rows; if not, identify a family forcing superpolynomial intermediate or certificate growth.
body.justification: The ordered exact-real theorem does not determine whether exact rational implementations remain output-polynomial in the ordinary Turing model.
body.gap: Bareiss1968SylvesterIdentity controls integer growth in one fraction-free elimination, but no located result controls simultaneous principal-regression keys, exact row equality certificates, and fragment tries over all \(2^p\) LiMVAM states.
body.consumer: Exact symbolic causal-discovery software needs a certified representation bound before the population enumerator can be advertised as polynomial-bit rather than unit-cost exact-real.
